meta.location: The wall of Zarahemla, and then the whole land
principles: A sermon that divides its hearers

world_behind.title: The crowd splits three ways
world_behind.text: Verse 1 has believers going to Nephi, verse 2 has others throwing stones and arrows, and verse 3 has more believing when the throwing fails.

world_behind.title: Nephi is already working
world_behind.text: Verses 4 and 5 have him baptizing, prophesying, showing signs, and telling people things in advance so they will remember being told.

world_behind.title: The failure to hit him is used as evidence against him
world_behind.text: Verse 6 has them concluding he has a devil, since nothing else explains the misses.

world_behind.title: Samuel leaves and is never mentioned again
world_behind.text: Verses 7 and 8 have him jumping off the wall, going home to preach, and dropping out of the Nephite record entirely.

world_behind.title: Four years pass with little change
world_behind.text: Verses 9 through 12 summarize the eighty-seventh through eighty-ninth years in three sentences.

world_behind.title: Angels appear to wise men
world_behind.text: Verse 14 reports it in the ninetieth year, in the language Luke 2:10 uses at Bethlehem.

world_behind.title: The unbelievers' reasoning is quoted in full
world_behind.text: Verses 16 through 21 give their argument, including a theory about priests keeping them ignorant.

words.text: A dismissive way of naming a man. The record uses the word eight times, including Mosiah 13:1, where Noah's priests call Abinadi "this fellow." The King James Bible has it twenty-eight times, often in the same register.
A change in condition. The word occurs once in all of scripture, here, where the record has almost nothing to report for a year.
Arrived at by chance rather than knowledge. The word occurs once in all of scripture, here, in the unbelievers' explanation of how the prophets could be right.
Lack of knowledge, here alleged as a condition imposed by others. The record uses the word seven times, twice in this chapter, and Alma 30:23 has Korihor making the same charge against the priests.
Beyond understanding, and in this verse suspiciously so. The word occurs once in all of scripture, in the phrase "the cunning and the mysterious arts of the evil one."
Reports spread without a source. The record uses the word eight times and the King James Bible never. Verse 22 makes Satan the one spreading them across the land.

phrases.term: As many as believed on his word went forth and sought for Nephi
phrases.text: The believers go looking for a different prophet. Samuel gave them the message and Nephi had the baptizing authority.

phrases.term: They could not hit him with their stones neither with their arrows
phrases.text: The event the whole chapter turns on. It is a miracle of failure rather than of display.

phrases.term: When they saw that they could not hit him, there were many more who did believe
phrases.text: One group's reading of the misses. Verse 6 gives another group's reading of the same fact.

phrases.term: That they might know and remember at the time of their coming that they had been made known unto them beforehand
phrases.text: Nephi's stated purpose in prophesying. The point of the advance notice is what it will mean afterward.

phrases.term: Take this fellow and bind him, for behold he hath a devil
phrases.text: The alternative explanation. The unexplained protection becomes proof of the opposite conclusion.

phrases.term: He did cast himself down from the wall, and did flee out of their lands
phrases.text: The exit. He goes home and preaches to his own people, and the record follows him no further.

phrases.term: He was never heard of more among the Nephites
phrases.text: The record closing a file. One of its most quoted prophets leaves in a single clause.

phrases.term: Angels did appear unto men, wise men, and did declare unto them glad tidings of great joy
phrases.text: Reported in the ninetieth year, in the same words Luke uses at Bethlehem. Both hemispheres get angels and wise men.

phrases.term: Some things they may have guessed right, among so many
phrases.text: The first argument: enough predictions will produce some hits. It concedes the accuracy and denies what it implies.

phrases.term: Why will he not show himself in this land as well as in the land of Jerusalem?
phrases.text: The second argument, and a fair question. 3 Nephi 11 answers it in about thirty years.

phrases.term: Thus will they keep us in ignorance if we will yield ourselves unto them
phrases.text: The third argument: the whole thing is a device for control. Korihor had made the same case in Alma 30:23.

verses.label: v. 1–5
verses.title: Believers and stones
verses.text: Many hear Samuel on the wall, and those who believe go to Nephi, confess their sins, and ask for baptism. Those who do not believe are angry and throw stones and shoot arrows, and the Spirit is with him so that nothing hits. Seeing that, many more believe and go to be baptized. Nephi is baptizing, prophesying, preaching repentance, showing signs and working miracles, so they will know Christ is coming shortly and will remember afterward that they had been told beforehand.

verses.label: v. 6–8
verses.title: The order and the escape
verses.text: The more part do not believe, and when the stones and arrows miss they call for their captains to bind him, saying he has a devil and that this is why they cannot hit him. As they move to take him he throws himself down from the wall and flees to his own country, where he preaches among his own people. He is never heard of again among the Nephites.

verses.label: v. 9–12
verses.title: Four quiet years
verses.text: The eighty-sixth year ends, and the eighty-seventh with the more part in pride and wickedness and a lesser part walking more circumspectly. The eighty-eighth is the same. In the eighty-ninth there is little alteration except that the people grow more hardened and do more against the commandments.

verses.label: v. 13–14
verses.title: The signs begin
verses.text: In the ninetieth year great signs and wonders are given and the words of the prophets begin to be fulfilled. Angels appear to men, to wise men, declaring glad tidings of great joy, and the scriptures begin to be fulfilled.

verses.label: v. 15–19
verses.title: The hardening and two arguments
verses.text: The people harden, except the most believing among Nephites and Lamanites, and begin to depend on their own strength and wisdom. They say some guesses landed among so many, and that the great works spoken of cannot happen. They reason and contend, asking why a Christ is reasonable at all, and why he would show himself at Jerusalem instead of here.

verses.label: v. 20–23
verses.title: The theory of control
verses.text: They call it a wicked tradition handed down to make them believe in something marvelous happening far away, where they cannot check it, so that the teachers can keep them in ignorance and dependent by mysterious arts. They imagine many foolish things and are disturbed, while Satan spreads rumors and contentions across the land and gets great hold on the people despite the signs and miracles.

verses.label: v. 24–25
verses.title: The close
verses.text: The ninetieth year ends, and so does the book of Helaman, according to the record of Helaman and his sons.

chapter.title: The same fact produces opposite conclusions
chapter.text: The stones miss. Verse 3 has people believing because of it and verse 6 has people diagnosing a devil because of it.

chapter.title: Belief sends them to a different man
chapter.text: Verse 1 has Samuel's converts going to find Nephi. The messenger and the ordinance are held by two people, and neither competes with the other.

chapter.title: The record loses track of its own prophet
chapter.text: Verse 8 says he was never heard of more. One of the most quoted figures in the book exits without a summary.

chapter.title: Almost nothing happens for four years
chapter.text: Verses 9 through 12 compress them into three sentences, and "little alteration" is the chapter's own phrase for it.

chapter.title: The unbelievers get a full hearing
chapter.text: Six verses are given to their reasoning in their own voice. Mormon quotes the case rather than only naming it.

chapter.title: The strongest objection is the fairest one
chapter.text: Verse 19 asks why Christ would appear at Jerusalem and not here. 3 Nephi 11 gives the answer, which nobody in this chapter lives to hear.

chapter.title: The theory of control is old
chapter.text: Alma 30:23 had Korihor arguing that priests keep the people in ignorance. The same case reappears sixty years later in the mouths of ordinary citizens.

chapter.title: The book ends in the year before the sign
chapter.text: The ninetieth year closes with Satan holding the hearts of the people, two years before the night with no darkness.

applications.title: Send people where the help actually is
applications.text: Samuel preached and pointed them to Nephi for baptism. Knowing which part of the work is yours is part of doing it.

applications.title: Notice when you are explaining away rather than explaining
applications.text: The misses got attributed to a devil. When a fact is inconvenient, watch for the account that keeps everything else unchanged.

applications.title: Take the good objection seriously
applications.text: Why here and not there is a real question. Dismissing the best version of an argument leaves it standing.

applications.title: Watch what happens when nothing happens
applications.text: "Little alteration" covered a year of quiet hardening. Drift does not announce itself.

questions.text: What evidence have I seen that changed my mind?
What have I attributed to a bad motive because the plain reading was inconvenient?
Who did the work in my life and then disappeared without credit?
What year of mine had little alteration, and what was happening under it?
Where am I calling a pattern a coincidence?
What is the strongest objection to something I believe?
Whose teaching do I resent depending on?
